title: Cloud & Supply Chain
description: Exploitation of cloud identity access policies, serverless runtimes, container isolation escapes, CI/CD pipelines, and third-party dependencies.

attacks.name: S3 bucket misconfiguration
attacks.desc: Misconfiguring AWS S3 bucket policies or Access Control Lists to allow public anonymous read, list, or write permissions, exposing proprietary objects or hosting malicious files.
attacks.prevention: Block public access by default, require least-privilege bucket policies, and review S3 access analyzer findings.

attacks.name: GCS bucket misconfiguration
attacks.desc: Granting Storage Object Viewer or Admin permissions to 'allUsers' or 'allAuthenticatedUsers' in Google Cloud Storage, leaking confidential corporate data.
attacks.prevention: Use uniform bucket-level access where appropriate and deny anonymous reads or writes unless explicitly intended.

attacks.name: Azure blob misconfiguration
attacks.desc: Setting Azure Blob storage container access levels to public, allowing anyone to enumerate, download, or overwrite stored enterprise blobs.
attacks.prevention: Disable anonymous blob access, use scoped identities, and review container-level permissions regularly.

attacks.name: IAM misconfiguration
attacks.desc: Granting excessive cloud permissions (e.g. sts:AssumeRole, iam:PassRole, admin wildcards) to service accounts or compute instances, facilitating lateral privilege escalation.
attacks.prevention: Grant identities only required actions and resources, separate roles by workload, and audit effective permissions.

attacks.name: Serverless function injection
attacks.desc: Injecting malicious command strings or template expressions into event parameters processed by AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions, or Azure Functions.
attacks.prevention: Validate serverless event input, avoid unsafe evaluation, and give the function a minimal execution role.

attacks.name: Lambda event injection
attacks.desc: Poisoning upstream event sources (such as SQS queues, S3 event notifications, or SNS topics) that trigger Lambda executions, executing commands in serverless execution environments.

attacks.name: Container escape
attacks.desc: Breaking out of isolated container runtimes into the host operating system by exploiting privileged container flags, mounted docker.sock, or kernel vulnerabilities (e.g. dirty COW, runc CVEs).

attacks.name: Kubernetes RBAC misconfig
attacks.desc: Assigning overly permissive Role or ClusterRole bindings (e.g. secrets get/list, pods/exec) to default service accounts within Kubernetes clusters.

attacks.name: Terraform state exposure
attacks.desc: Leaving unencrypted Terraform state files (.tfstate) in public buckets or version control, exposing plaintext database passwords, cloud secrets, and private keys.

attacks.name: CI/CD pipeline injection
attacks.desc: Injecting malicious commands into GitHub Actions workflows or GitLab CI jobs via untrusted pull request titles, issue comments, or poisoned branch names.

attacks.name: Dependency confusion
attacks.desc: Publishing public packages to open registries (npm, PyPI) matching private internal package names, tricking enterprise build pipelines into downloading malicious public packages.

attacks.name: Typosquatted packages
attacks.desc: Registering package names that visually or phonetically mimic popular open-source libraries (e.g. cross-env vs crossenv) to deliver backdoored packages to inattentive developers.

attacks.name: Malicious npm/pip package
attacks.desc: Compromising legitimate maintainer accounts or transferring package ownership to inject backdoors, crypto miners, or credential exfiltration code into popular library updates.

attacks.name: Build script RCE
attacks.desc: Exploiting automated package installation lifecycle hooks (e.g. npm postinstall scripts, pip setup.py) to execute arbitrary malicious code upon package download.
